paper_metadata.title: The effect of the combustion channels on the compressive strength of porous NiTi shape memory alloy fabricated by SHS as implant material
paper_metadata.journal: Current Opinion in Solid State and Materials Science

evidence.quote: Porous NiTi shape memory alloy (SMA) with ideal porosity and high compressive strength as an implant material was fabricated by self-propagating high-temperature synthesis (SHS).

The raw materials used were Ni (99.8 wt%) and Ti (99.5 wt%) powders with an average size of /C0 44 lm (Alfa Aesar). The mixed powders of Ni and Ti with 50.5 at.%Ni were blended in a rotating container for 24 h for a homogenous mixture.
Then the blended powder was pressed into cylindrical compacts of 10 mm in diameter using a hydraulic press at a cold compaction pressure of 100 MPa. The green porosity of specimens was 50.5 vol%.
The green specimens then were preheated up to 350 /C176C with approximately 15 /C176C/min heating rate in a furnace under the protection of high purity argon gas
subjected to electrical discharge pulse (14 kV and 30 mA) [25] and then synthesized by igniting at different locations to obtain combustion channels differently oriented.
